estimate.damage_summary: During a swerve on the Berlin–Munich drive, the laptop was thrown against the car door, cracking its screen and damaging its lower-right corner. The invoice describes screen and housing repairs, a polish of a pre-existing lid scuff, and a diagnostic inspection.
estimate.policy_notes: The described sudden impact during a vehicle manoeuvre is covered under 2.6.1–2.6.2, and portable equipment temporarily away from the insured location in Germany is covered under 4.5.2; this assessment assumes the stated portable electronics cover and household-property co-insurance are agreed in the schedule. Necessary repairs are limited to event-damaged areas and the pre-loss standard under 7.1.5, 7.1.7 and 7.1.9; examination is covered under 5.2.3, subject to its EUR 250 gross cap per event. Polishing the pre-existing scuff is excluded under 7.1.11 and 7.1.8(a). No deductible or proportional reduction is specified in the supplied documents.

lines.rationale: The screen cracked in the reported sudden impact, so repair of that affected area is covered under 2.6.1–2.6.3 and 7.1.5; the complete display assembly is a plausible repair method for the cracked screen. Under 7.1.7 and 7.1.9, the reasonable amount is limited to a standard-equivalent display repair for this 14-inch notebook, not an upgrade; one screen repair is justified, with the description indicating this is the larger share of the repair cost.

The lower-right housing damage is expressly attributed to the same impact, and repair of that affected part is covered under 2.6.1–2.6.3 and 7.1.5. Replacing the dented housing shell is a plausible necessary repair under 7.1.7, subject to the equivalent pre-loss standard in 7.1.9; one repair is justified and its reasonable price should remain below the display repair.

lines.invoice_text: Polish of pre-existing lid scuff (surface only, does not affect operation)
lines.rationale: The description identifies this as a pre-existing cosmetic scuff, not damage caused by the insured event, so it is outside the affected areas under 7.1.5 and is not a repair cost under 7.1.11 and 7.1.8(a). The line is unrelated to making good the screen or corner impact; one polish is the stated quantity, and its price estimate is given only on the assumption it were valid.

The inspection was performed to establish the extent and scope of repair for an insured portable-equipment event, so it falls under 5.2.3, which expressly includes the repairing undertaking’s diagnostic charge. One inspection is justified; a modest charge for a short diagnostic is reasonable, and reimbursement remains subject to the EUR 250 gross per-event cap in 5.2.3.
